note: Generated by scripts/map.mjs. Machine-readable reload for agents; see PROJECT_MAP.md for prose.

project.name: brewdocs
project.tagline: Brew your docs, serve them hot.
project.what:
A zero-config documentation generator for code. Point it at a local path, an npm package name, or a GitHub URL and it produces one self-contained HTML page (plus a queryable `docmodel.json`). It also ships a hosting server, a CLI with coverage/diff/gate tooling, language adapters beyond JS/TS, and an MCP server so agents can read the same model.

The product's whole job is rendering prose from repositories **you do not own** — READMEs, doc comments, git tag names. That is the threat model everything in `facts/invariants.json` follows from.
project.audience: Maintainers of the monorepo and anyone hosting `brewdocs serve` on a reachable address.

invariants.rule: The hosting server binds 127.0.0.1 unless the operator passes --host. A non-loopback bind with no token and no keys mints a token before serving.
invariants.why: `server.listen(port)` binds every interface on Node. The build API can run npm install, so an open instance on a LAN is remote code execution, and the startup banner used to say 'localhost' while the socket said otherwise.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (source confinement), packages/cli/src/cli-commands.test.ts (isLoopbackHost)

invariants.rule: Fetching an npm package must pass --ignore-scripts and must not pass the parent process environment through to the child.
invariants.why: BrewDocs only needs a package's README and source to build docs. Lifecycle scripts (postinstall et al.) are arbitrary code execution from a caller-supplied name, reachable from the build API.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/test/resolve.test.ts

invariants.rule: Every endpoint that reads a caller-supplied local path must resolve it against sourceRoot and refuse anything outside with 403. Realpath first, so neither .. nor a symlink escapes.
invariants.why: A build endpoint that renders any readable directory is a file-disclosure primitive; /api/export returned the HTML directly, so a README containing a key was disclosed verbatim.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (Phase 5 — source confinement)

invariants.rule: HTML escaping has one implementation (packages/core/src/escape.ts) that escapes " and ' as well as & < >, because untrusted values are interpolated into quoted attributes (href, value, title).
invariants.why: This is the contract, not one call site. The XSS shipped because escapeHtml escaped only &<>; local copies then multiplied (highlight, workspaces, registry, federation) and the gate only checked three fixed files. One source plus an all-files scan keeps a new quote-blind helper from slipping in.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/src/escape.ts (the single escaper) + scripts/gate.mjs (inv-4:escape-helpers-quote-safe scans every source file) + packages/core/test/escape.test.ts

invariants.rule: Path containment must be boundary-aware: resolve the candidate and require it to equal the root or start with root + path.sep. Never use a bare startsWith.
invariants.why: startsWith accepted a sibling whose name shared the target's prefix (/s/acme/../acme-secret resolved outside hosting/acme). The existing traversal test passed for the wrong reason — Node's URL normalizer, not the code.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (prefix-confusion, dots-only subdomains)

invariants.rule: A site subdomain must be a plain DNS-ish slug; dots-only and separator-bearing values are refused before any path resolution.
invariants.why: The Host header is caller-controlled and `...brewdocs.dev` slugifies to `..`, which reaches above the hosting directory.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (rejects dots-only / separator-bearing subdomains)

invariants.rule: A URL placed in href/src must have its scheme validated; javascript:, vbscript: and data: are dropped, including control-character-smuggled forms.
invariants.why: Markdown link targets come from third-party prose. `java\nscript:` is still javascript: to a browser, so the scheme check must strip control characters before sniffing.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/test/markdown.test.ts

invariants.rule: Any writer that takes a site-root-relative path from config must resolve it against the output directory and refuse anything outside. Same boundary-aware rule as INV-5: no bare startsWith.
invariants.why: `redirects:` and `aliases:` in brewdocs.yml are repo-controlled, so a `from: "../x.html"` key could create files above the build output. Reachable from any repo you build docs for.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/test/aliases.test.ts (v3.8 containment of generated output)

invariants.rule: A theme slot partial path must be confined to the manifest's source root before it is read.
invariants.why: Slot values are repo-controlled config. A `themes/brand.yml` shipped by the repo being documented could name `../../id_rsa`; the build would read it and can embed it in a page the user then publishes.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/plugin-sdk/test/v2.test.ts (confines slot partials to the source root)

invariants.rule: A POST (write) request must be refused with 403 when the browser signals a cross-site origin: Origin must equal the Host we were reached on, and Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin or none.
invariants.why: Any web page can POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request and no preflight. Non-browser clients send neither header and stay allowed.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (refuses cross-site POST /api/build)

invariants.rule: CI workflows must install with npm ci, never npm install.
invariants.why: A lockfile-ignoring install on a tree containing package.json scripts is a supply-chain surface; the Pages workflow ran on a repository with pages: write and id-token: write granted.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-11:ci-uses-npm-ci)

invariants.rule: The published @brewdocs/core must resolve to compiled JS (dist/), not raw TypeScript, so a plain-Node consumer can import it.
invariants.why: Core shipped src/**/*.ts; `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node threw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. Dev/test keep using source via tsconfig paths + a vitest alias, so only the published entry changes.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-12:core-ships-compiled) + CI pack smoke

invariants.rule: A per-user API key must only perform the operations its scopes include; a write endpoint with the wrong scope returns 403.
invariants.why: keys.ts stored and printed scopes that server.ts never read, so a `--scope build` key could export and render markdown too. The surface advertised a boundary it did not have.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (enforces the key's scopes per write endpoint)

invariants.rule: A release tag must run the verify gate (typecheck + map + security invariants + tests) before publishing.
invariants.why: publish.yml published three packages on any v* tag after only `npm ci` + `npm test`; provenance attests where it was built, not that it works.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-14:release-runs-verify)

invariants.rule: X-Forwarded-For may only set the rate-limit client identity behind an explicit opt-in (trustProxy / BREWDOCS_TRUST_PROXY=1); otherwise the socket address is used.
invariants.why: The header is caller-controlled, so honouring it unconditionally let a client defeat the only brake on the expensive /api/build path by rotating the value.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-15:trust-proxy-opt-in)

invariants.rule: Read endpoints that expose deployment/registry/federation metadata must 401 once auth is configured (admin token or keys); only a fully unauthenticated instance leaves them open.
invariants.why: needsAuth was driven by the token alone, so an instance with keys but no BREWDOCS_TOKEN leaked /api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search and the stats rollup anonymously.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-16:read-endpoints-guarded) + packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (guards read endpoints once auth is configured)

invariants.rule: An adapter that executes code against the source tree (python) must refuse a fetched (npm/git) source and run only for a locally chosen one.
invariants.why: The python adapter shells out to a bundled AST helper; running it against a package the user did not choose turns a doc build into code execution on attacker-supplied input.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-17:python-refuses-fetched)

invariants.rule: The renderer must have a golden-output snapshot test over a full page, including hostile inputs.
invariants.why: A renderer that emits its own CSS/JS had no output test, which is how the attribute-injection XSS (#3) survived hundreds of green unit tests that only checked substrings.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-18:renderer-golden)

invariants.rule: Every write endpoint (POST) must carry an explicit guard (authorize / guardSource / requireSiteAccess) before it acts on caller input.
invariants.why: The build/export/markdown APIs are the RCE and file-disclosure surface. A new POST route added without a guard would ship open; the gate asserts the guard from the routes it parses out of server.ts.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-19:write-endpoints-guarded)

invariants.rule: A fetched (npm/git) source must not be able to name its own plugins: plugins listed in the source's brewdocs.yml are ignored unless the source was chosen locally. Plugins the operator passed explicitly (--plugins) still load.
invariants.why: A plugin is arbitrary code — loaded via require/import, with no signature and no sandbox. The specifier is read from the source's own brewdocs.yml, and BrewDocs' stated job is rendering repos you do not own, so honoring it turns every doc build into remote code execution on the operator's machine. This is the same threat INV-17 already refuses for the python adapter, in a wider blast radius. The subtle part is propagation:  must survive every hop from resolveInput to resolveSetup, and each hop that rebuilt a Source without it silently re-enabled the repo's plugins. That is how the first version of this fix was bypassed three times (per-version worktree, extractVersion, and the CLI build command) before the gate check was written to assert all of them.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/test/plugin-fetched.test.ts + scripts/gate.mjs (inv-20:fetched-source-cannot-name-plugins, which asserts the guard and every Source re-construction site)

invariants.rule: The HTTP MCP transport (POST /mcp?site=<sub>) must be gated like the other reads — 401 once auth is configured, and a private site additionally requires its access token — and it must record every tools/call into the analytics store.
invariants.why: This endpoint exposes a site's docmodel to agents, so an unauthenticated caller on a server with auth configured must not reach it, and a private site's docs must not leak through the agent-shaped door when they are closed on the HTML door. Recording the call is the endpoint's whole purpose: without it, the product never learns which symbols were asked for and not found, which is the gap this release exists to close.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-21:mcp-http-guarded) + packages/cli/src/mcp-http.test.ts (auth, private-site token, telemetry round-trip)

invariants.rule: The stdio and HTTP MCP transports must answer through one shared message handler; a tool added or changed must behave identically on both.
invariants.why: Two transports over the same protocol is exactly the shape that lets a fix land in one path and not the other — the same failure mode that let the plugin 'fetched' guard be bypassed three times (INV-20). One handler means the protocol has a single implementation to keep correct.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-22:mcp-one-protocol-handler) + packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts (handleMcpMessage is the single dispatcher)

invariants.rule: Every comparison against a credential (token, token hash, key hash, domain verification token) must go through safeEqual in core/src/compare.ts — never a bare === — and safeEqual must never throw on a length mismatch.
invariants.why: A === on a secret is not guaranteed constant-time, so each compared byte leaks a little timing signal (finding #20). The sites were spread across four modules (server.ts site access, the admin Bearer compares, cloud.ts org membership, keys.ts key lookup, domains.ts verification token), which is the same one-fix-many-copies shape as the escaping bug (INV-4) — so the gate scans every source file for a secret-ish identifier beside ===/!==, not a fixed file list. The wrapper (rather than a raw crypto.timingSafeEqual) is load-bearing: timingSafeEqual throws RangeError on a length mismatch, and a throw in this server exits the process (finding #21), so the naive swap would have traded a timing leak for an unauthenticated crash.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-23:credentials-compared-in-constant-time) + packages/core/test/compare.test.ts (length mismatch, UTF-8 semantics, non-strings) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (wrong-length token over HTTP)

invariants.rule: A single request must not be able to kill the process: every request listener is guarded, caller-controlled parsing (the request line, percent-decoding) answers 400, and every file stream handles its own error.
invariants.why: An async request listener that throws rejects a promise with no handler attached and Node exits the process; a synchronous listener that throws does the same. Requests are untrusted input, so one malformed request line (GET //[ — new URL() throws) or one client that abandons a POST mid-body (the body read throws aborted) was an unauthenticated denial of service against both the hosting server and the preview server (finding #21, reproduced by execution). An unhandled error on fs.createReadStream(...).pipe(res) is the same class: a file that vanishes between the existence check and the open takes the process with it.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-24:request-cannot-kill-the-process) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (hostile request line, lone percent-escape, aborted body, wrong-length token — each asserts the next request still answers 200)

invariants.rule: A stored credential hash must not authenticate: authentication hashes what it is presented, while only operator-side mutations (add/remove member) may accept an already-hashed value.
invariants.why: canAccessOrg used normalizeKeyHash, which passes a non-bd_live_ string through untouched, so presenting a member's stored keyHash back as the Bearer token returned 200 (finding #22, reproduced over HTTP). The stored hash is an artifact at rest; if it is also a credential then hashing buys nothing and anyone who can read .cloud.json holds every member key in usable form. validateKey in keys.ts never had the hole (it always hashes, so a hash double-hashes and misses) — the two key stores disagreed about what a credential is, which is why the asymmetry stayed invisible.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-25:stored-hash-is-not-a-credential) + packages/core/test/cloud.test.ts (stored hash rejected, raw key still accepted)

invariants.rule: A site manifest that exists but cannot be read must fail closed: only ENOENT is 'missing' (benign), every other read or parse failure is 'unreadable' and every consumer refuses.
invariants.why: deploySite and setDraftExpiry rewrite .brewdocs.json with a plain non-atomic writeFileSync, so a crash or a full disk leaves a truncated file; readManifest used to answer undefined for every failure and requireSiteAccess reads an absent tokenHash as public, so a damaged manifest silently published a private site (finding #23, reproduced: 401 intact, 200 truncated, same anonymous request). The states are deliberately distinct: a MISSING manifest stays benign (a hand-dropped directory serves as public, D-12) because whoever can delete the manifest can equally rewrite its visibility — absence is not the weakness, an unreadable file is, because the file's real contents are unknown rather than 'public'.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-26:damaged-manifest-fails-closed) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (truncated manifest refused on the site route, /mcp, /dashboard and /api/stats; listed as private in /api/sites; repairing the file restores service)

invariants.rule: A site name taken from ?site= must pass the same slug guard as routing (SAFE_SUBDOMAIN) before any filesystem access; readManifest is the chokepoint and /mcp builds its docmodel path only after the manifest read succeeds.
invariants.why: resolveSite validated /s/ and Host routing but the query-param routes (/mcp, /dashboard, /api/stats) passed the raw parameter to path.join, so ?site=../sibling read a directory above the hosting root — 200 on /mcp with its docmodel and the outside title rendered by /dashboard (finding #24, reproduced). The two routing forms and the three query-param forms must agree about what a site name is; validating inside readManifest makes that structural instead of five copies of the same check.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-27:site-param-cannot-leave-hosting) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (?site=../outside answers 404 on /mcp and /dashboard, and the outside title never renders)

invariants.rule: A private site is always token-gated: every private deploy records a tokenHash, and a private manifest without one is refused rather than read as public.
invariants.why: requireSiteAccess treated an absent tokenHash as 'nothing to check' — but private: true in brewdocs.yml set visibility without minting a token (only the --private/--draft flags minted), so the documented config path produced a private site that served anonymously (finding #25, reproduced by execution; the CLI even printed 'token: undefined'). Both halves are needed: the CLI mint keeps new deploys correct, and the server refusal is the backstop for hand-edited and pre-fix manifests, which would otherwise stay open forever.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-28:private-site-always-token-gated) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (hashless private manifest refused on /s/, /dashboard and /mcp) + packages/cli/src/cli-commands.test.ts (private: true in config records a tokenHash)

invariants.rule: An unreadable key store counts as 'auth IS configured', not as 'no auth': needsAuth is true while .keys.json exists but does not parse as an array, and every gated route refuses until it is repaired.
invariants.why: loadKeys degrades every failure to [] and needsAuth was Boolean(token) || loadKeys(...).length > 0, so a damaged store read as 'no auth configured' and every gated read and write answered anonymously — reproduced with a corrupt store (GET /api/sites -> 200) and with {} (POST /api/export -> 200) (finding #26). This is the authorization twin of the manifest fail-open (#23): a store that cannot be read must refuse, not default to open. loadKeys also no longer hands a non-array document to callers, where {} used to reach .find and throw.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-29:unreadable-key-store-refuses) + packages/cli/src/v46.test.ts (corrupt store: /api/sites and /api/build answer 401, and the previously valid key cannot authenticate either)

invariants.rule: A theme manifest's vars and css must not be able to terminate the <style> element: '<' is neutralized before interpolation.
invariants.why: HTML ends a raw-text <style> element at the literal sequence '</style', and escapeHtml cannot help inside a raw-text element. themeVars and the manifest css string were interpolated raw, so a repo shipping themes/brand.yml with vars: { accent: '</style><script>…' } got a live script in the built page (finding #27, reproduced by execution). cssSafe in render.ts neutralizes '<' into the CSS escape '\3c ', keeping the style element intact.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-30:style-channel-cannot-break-out) + packages/core/test/hostile.test.ts (hostile manifest vars and css produce no live script and style count is 1)

findings.title: serve bound every interface with auth off (RCE via npm postinstall)
Unauthenticated build API rendered any absolute local path
Attribute injection / XSS: escapeHtml did not escape quotes
resolveSite prefix-confusion read sibling sites
Subdomain `..` escaped the hosting dir; CLI --name was never slugified
findings.detail: Server-side slug guard landed in v3.7.0 (checkedBy inv-6). The CLI deploy path now always routes the requested name through combineSubdomain, so `brewdocs deploy --name ../x` slugifies to `x` instead of writing outside the hosting dir.

findings.title: emitRedirects wrote outside outDir via a `from: "../x"` key
findings.detail: Reachable from any repo's brewdocs.yml (`redirects:`). The `skip: file exists` guard prevented overwriting but not creating outside the output tree. emitAliasPages was checked at the same time: its alias name goes through dirSafe, which maps separators to `_`, so it could not traverse â€” but the write target is now confirmed inside outDir anyway.

findings.title: publish.yml publishes on any v* tag with no typecheck or smoke build
findings.detail: publish.yml ran only `npm ci` + `npm test`, so a tag on a commit whose types do not compile still published three packages. It now runs `npm run verify` (typecheck + map + gate + tests) plus a smoke build before any publish. Provenance attests where it was built, not that it works.

findings.title: @brewdocs/core ships raw TypeScript; plain Node cannot import it
findings.detail: Core shipped raw src/**/*.ts, so `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node threw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. It now builds to dist (tsconfig.build.json, excluding tests), ships dist/ with a types+import exports map, and builds via prepublishOnly. Dev, tests and typecheck still resolve workspace source through tsconfig paths + a vitest alias, so the CLI keeps running TS directly (D-2).

findings.title: API key scopes are stored and printed but never enforced
findings.detail: keys.ts persisted and printed `scopes` but server.ts never read them, so a `--scope build` key performed every operation. Write endpoints now call authorize(req, scope) and return 403 when the key's scopes do not include build/export/markdown; the admin token still grants all, and a key with no scopes means all (keys.ts).

findings.title: Rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally
findings.detail: clientKey() trusted X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, so rotating the header defeated the limiter. It now keys on the socket address unless the operator opts in via ProtectionOptions.trustProxy / BREWDOCS_TRUST_PROXY=1.

findings.title: Analytics/registry endpoints leak when keys exist but no admin token is set
findings.detail: needsAuth was driven by the token, so with keys present and BREWDOCS_TOKEN unset, /api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search and the /api/stats rollup answered unauthenticated. They now call authorizeRead and 401 unless the admin token or a valid key is presented; with no auth configured at all they stay open for the local drop-in UI.

findings.title: Theme slot partials resolved relative to the manifest (arbitrary file read)
findings.detail: A themes/brand.yml committed by a repo owner could name a slot value like ../../id_rsa; manifestSlots() read it and the build could embed it in a published page. Slot partials are now confined to the manifest's source root (recorded by loadThemeManifest as `sourceRoot`), boundary-aware in the same way as INV-5.

findings.title: Pages workflow uses npm install instead of npm ci
findings.detail: .github/workflows/brewdocs.yml ran `npm install` on a tree that contains package.json scripts, with pages: write + id-token: write granted. It now uses `npm ci`; the gate refuses any workflow that reintroduces `npm install`.

findings.title: Doc/reality drift (test counts, root package version, gitignored roadmap)
findings.detail: Test counts, file/LOC totals and the HTTP surface table are now parsed by scripts/map.mjs instead of typed, and CI fails when the map is stale. The root package.json version now tracks the three workspaces (4.1.0). ROADMAP.md remains gitignored by design (it is local planning, like AGENTS.md and the release notes).

findings.title: python adapter executes a bundled helper against the target tree
findings.detail: The python adapter executes a bundled AST helper against the tree. Sources fetched from npm/git are now flagged Source.fetched, propagated to AdapterContext, and the adapter refuses (warn + skip) rather than running against code the user did not choose locally.

findings.title: No CSRF/Origin check on write endpoints
findings.detail: Any web page could POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request (no preflight). POST endpoints now 403 when Origin does not match the Host, or Sec-Fetch-Site is not same-origin/none. Non-browser clients send neither header and are unaffected.

findings.title: No golden-output test for the renderer
findings.detail: The renderer emits its own CSS/JS and had no golden-output test, which is how the attribute-injection XSS (#3) survived 311 green tests. render.golden.test.ts now snapshots a full deterministic page with a hostile link/description, so an escaping regression fails loudly.

findings.title: api.test.ts was flaky under load (2 tests at a 30s timeout)
findings.detail: A full-suite run on 2026-09-26 failed two endpoint tests at 31.2s / 33.9s against `{ timeout: 30_000 }`; a solo run of the file passed in 28.7s and an immediate re-run of the full suite went green. Both tests do a full TS extraction synchronously, so they are sensitive to load. Found by running the suite while building the map generator.

findings.title: A fetched repo brewdocs.yml could name a plugin, executing arbitrary code at build time (RCE)
findings.detail: Reproduced by execution on 2026-09-28, not inferred: a synthetic repo whose brewdocs.yml contained plugins: [./pwn.cjs], with the plugin writing a marker file, ran that code during brewdocs build. loadPlugin resolves the specifier with requireFrom(root)(abs) — no signature, no sandbox — and build.ts called loadPlugins(config.plugins, ...) with no check of source.fetched. The guard for this class already existed and was simply not applied: finding #15 / INV-17 made the python adapter refuse a fetched source for exactly this reason. Three further bypasses were found while fixing it, all the same root cause (a Source rebuilt without carrying fetched): the per-version worktree in buildVersions, the extractVersion checkout, and the CLI build command resolveCliSource, which dropped the flag on the main brewdocs build path. All four sites now propagate fetched and resolveSetup drops repo-config plugins for a fetched source. Operator-passed --plugins still load, since that is the caller own choice, and a locally chosen source is unaffected.

findings.title: Credentials were compared with === (not constant-time)
findings.detail: requireSiteAccess compared the sha256 of a presented token with the stored tokenHash using === (server.ts), and the same shape appeared at every other credential site: the admin-token Bearer compares in authorize/authorizeRead, the site-org membership check in canAccessOrg, the API-key lookup in validateKey/revokeKey/claimSite, and the custom-domain verification token in verifyDomain. String comparison in JS is not guaranteed constant-time, so each byte leaks a little timing signal; with a high-entropy digest the practical exploitability is very low, which is why this is low severity, but the canonical hardening is cheap. All sites now route through one helper, safeEqual (core/src/compare.ts), which wraps crypto.timingSafeEqual. The wrapper exists because timingSafeEqual throws RangeError on a length mismatch — and a throw in this server exits the process (finding #21), so a naive swap would have traded a timing leak for an unauthenticated crash. safeEqual returns false instead, keeps === semantics (byte comparison, not digest comparison, so passing a pre-hashed value never silently becomes valid), and answers false for non-strings. Verified by execution, not inference: the scan that found these sites is now gate check inv-23, and the swap was proven by mutation (reverting any one site turns the gate red).

findings.title: One malformed request could kill the process (async handler throw)
findings.detail: Found while fixing #20: the swap to crypto.timingSafeEqual would have thrown RangeError on any wrong-length token, and that throw would have exited the server. Reproduced by execution: an async http request listener that throws rejects a promise with no handler attached, and Node exits the process (verified against the real server with a hostile request line, GET //[ — new URL() throws ERR_INVALID_URL before any route runs). Three distinct surfaces had the same defect class: buildRequestHandler (async, so any throw anywhere in any route kills the process), serveStatic in cli/src/index.ts (a synchronous listener, same outcome on a bad request line or a lone % in decodeURIComponent), and fs.createReadStream(...).pipe(res) on both static paths (a file removed between the existence check and the open emits unhandled error → process exit; verified with a stream to a missing file). Fixed with a single try/catch wrapper around the shared route body plus a 400 for the unparseable request line, a 400 in the preview server, and error handlers on both streams. A client that abandons a POST mid-body (the body read throws aborted) now yields a clean response instead of a crash. Verified by execution: hostile request lines, aborted bodies, and a wrong-length site token all leave the server answering 200 on the next request.

findings.title: A stored API-key hash authenticated as a credential (pass-the-hash)
findings.detail: Found while auditing the comparison sites for #20, and reproduced by execution over HTTP, not inferred: create an org, add a member with a raw bd_live_ key, read the member keyHash out of .cloud.json, then GET a private org site with Authorization: Bearer <that hash> — the server answered 200. Mechanism: canAccessOrg used normalizeKeyHash, which passes a non-bd_live_ string through untouched because that convenience exists for addOrgMember/removeOrgMember (an operator may paste either form). Authentication is different: the stored hash is an artifact at rest, and if presenting it back is sufficient then hashing buys nothing — anyone who can read .cloud.json (a backup, a synced folder, a hosting dir served or copied by mistake) holds every member credential in usable form. validateKey in cli/src/keys.ts never had this hole (it always hashes what it is presented, so the hash double-hashes and misses), which is why the asymmetry went unnoticed: the two key stores disagreed about what a credential is. Fixed by hashing in canAccessOrg (hashKey, not normalizeKeyHash), with the reason written at the call site. addOrgMember/removeOrgMember keep accepting a hash, because there the caller is the operator, not a request. Tests: packages/core/test/cloud.test.ts asserts the stored hash is rejected and the raw key still works.

findings.title: A damaged site manifest silently published a private site
findings.detail: Found by auditing an external handout claim that readManifest swallowing all errors was diagnostic friction; reproduced by execution it is an authorization fail-open. deploySite writes .brewdocs.json with a plain non-atomic writeFileSync (deploy.ts; setDraftExpiry rewrites the same file the same way), so a crash, a full disk, or two overlapping deploys leaves a truncated file. readManifest answered undefined for every failure and requireSiteAccess reads an absent tokenHash as public — so against the intact manifest the same anonymous GET answered 401, and after truncating the file it answered 200 with the page (reproduced against a real server; the same state also silently defeated draft expiry and the private dashboard/stats/mcp gates). Fixed by making readManifest three-state: ok / missing / unreadable, where only ENOENT is missing and a parse failure, a non-object document, or any other read error is unreadable; every consumer (site serve, /mcp, /dashboard, /api/stats) refuses with 500 on unreadable, and /api/sites lists such a site as private rather than public. A missing manifest stays benign on purpose (D-12). The refusal is announced on stderr and the state is visible in /api/sites, because the original complaint — a damaged file being indistinguishable from a missing one — was a real diagnostic defect too.

findings.title: ?site= walked outside the hosting dir on /mcp and /dashboard
findings.detail: The ?site= query parameter on /mcp, /dashboard and /api/stats was passed to readManifest and then to path.join unvalidated, so ?site=../sibling resolved above the hosting dir — the same boundary resolveSite already enforces for /s/ and Host routing (findings #4, #5), missing on the query-param routes. Reproduced with a second site directory outside the hosting dir: POST /mcp?site=../sibling answered 200 with its docmodel (tools/list), GET /dashboard?site=../sibling rendered its manifest title, and /api/stats read its manifest for the private gate. Private targets were still 401 (the manifest read found the real tokenHash), so the leak was the metadata and docmodels of directories outside the hosting root. Fixed at the chokepoint: readManifest validates the subdomain with SAFE_SUBDOMAIN — the same slug guard resolveSite applies — and answers missing for anything else, and the /mcp route now reads the manifest before it constructs the docmodel path, so that path is only ever built for a validated slug.

findings.title: A private site with no tokenHash served anonymously (private: true config minted no token)
findings.detail: Found while reproducing #23: a manifest that says visibility: private with no tokenHash served anonymously, because requireSiteAccess read an absent tokenHash as 'nothing to check, so public'. deploySite only records a tokenHash when a token is passed, and the CLI minted one only for the --private/--draft flags — private: true in brewdocs.yml (a documented config key) set visibility without minting, so the documented config path produced a private site the server could not gate, and the CLI printed 'Private site. Access with token: undefined'. Reproduced by execution: deploy with config private:true -> manifest has no tokenHash -> anonymous GET /s/<site>/ answered 200. Fixed in both halves. CLI: a token is minted whenever visibility resolves to private, not only for the flag. Server: requireSiteAccess refuses a private manifest with no tokenHash instead of reading it as public (the backstop for hand-edited or pre-fix manifests); the admin token and org members still pass, everyone else gets 401 until the site is redeployed.

findings.title: An unreadable key store turned every gated endpoint public
findings.detail: Found while auditing the sibling failure mode of #23. loadKeys degrades every failure to [] — invalid JSON, a non-array document, an unreadable file — and needsAuth is Boolean(token) || loadKeys(...).length > 0, so a damaged .keys.json read as 'no auth is configured' and every gated endpoint answered anonymously: reads (/api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search, /api/gap, /api/stats) and writes (/api/build, /api/export, /api/markdown), because authorize() returns ok when needsAuth is false. Reproduced: add a key, corrupt .keys.json, GET /api/sites -> 200; with the store set to {} (valid JSON, not an array) POST /api/export with any key -> 200. saveKeys writes the store with a plain non-atomic writeFileSync, so the trigger is the same partial-write class as #23. Fixed with keysStoreUnreadable(): an existing store that does not read back as an array counts as 'auth IS configured but unverifiable' — needsAuth is true and every gated route refuses (401) until the store is repaired, with a stderr line at server start and an error from `brewdocs keys list` so the operator sees why. loadKeys also stops handing a non-array document to callers ({} used to reach .find and throw).

findings.title: A theme manifest could end the <style> element and inject script into the page
findings.detail: Found by execution while writing the hostile-input property test the fuzz rename called for: a theme manifest is repo-controlled config (the same threat model as the slot-partial read, #9), and its vars and css values were interpolated into <style> without escaping '<' — so a repo shipping themes/brand.yml with vars: { accent: '</style><script>…</script>' } (or css: with the same) closed the style element and left a live script in the rendered page (reproduced by execution). The built-in themes are unaffected; the channel is theme manifests, the same repo-controlled config surface as #9. Fixed at the render chokepoint: cssSafe() neutralizes '<' into '\3c ' (the CSS hex escape) for var keys, var values and the css blob — a '<' has no business in CSS, and it is the only way out of the raw-text element. The property test in hostile.test.ts asserts hostile manifest vars and css produce no injected script and the <style> block is not prematurely closed.
